newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends quiet session moderately higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends quiet session moderately higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended slightly higher Friday, bouncing back modestly from Thursday's steep decline, but traders said today's move lacked momentum.
Turnover was thin at an estimated 4,602 lots, they said, and prices were confined to a tight range.
Dealers said trade buying accounted for the bulk of the day's gains, with local participation seen on both sides of the market.
Most-active March ended up 0.65 cent at 109.50 cents a lb after ranging from 109.80 to 108.55. Spot December futures finished 1.00 higher at 118.25, with the rest up 0.75 to 1.50.
The December/March switch widened to 8.75 cents from 8.40 cents at the close Thursday, while March/May narrowed slightly to 2.35 cents from 2.45 cents.

Open interest in the December contract, which entered notice period Tuesday and expires December 18, fell by 233 lots on Thursday, but remained relatively high at 1,766 lots, the equivalent of more than 400,000 bags of coffee.
As of Friday, no delivery notices had been issued.
On the charts, traders pegged March resistance at 111.00 cents, followed by 115.00 cents. Near-term support seen at 108.00-107.50 cents.

Elsewhere, industry representatives of Brazil's coffee community will meet in the state of Bahia next week to discuss the way forward for Brazil's coffee policy. The forum will take place from Nov 27 to Dec 1 near Ilheus in Bahia.
